topic: How to balance your radiators
facebook:
♨️ One room roasting, another one never warm? Your radiators probably need balancing — not replacing.

Here's what's happening. Hot water is lazy. It takes the easiest route, so the rads nearest the boiler hog it and the far ones get the leftovers.

Balancing just slows the greedy ones down so everything gets a fair share:

🔧 Open every lockshield valve fully, run the heating, note which rads warm first
🔧 Close the lockshield on the fastest rad almost shut, then open it about a quarter turn
🔧 Work outwards, giving the furthest rads the most flow
🔧 Give it an hour and check again

It costs nothing but an afternoon, and it's the single most overlooked fix in British heating.

Save this for when you need it.

topic: Why your pipes bang and creak at night
facebook:
🌙 Pipes banging and ticking after you've gone to bed? It's almost never haunted. It's usually one of four things.

🔨 Water hammer — a bang when a tap or the washing machine shuts off. The water was moving, then suddenly wasn't, and the shock has nowhere to go. A properly-fitted arrestor kills it.
🎵 Ticking as the heating goes off — copper expanding and contracting, rubbing against a floor joist or a clip that's too tight. Annoying, harmless, fixable.
🌊 Gurgling — air in the system. Bleed the rads.
🫧 A constant hiss or trickle when nothing's running — that one's not harmless. Something is passing water somewhere. Get it looked at.

Three of those you can live with. The fourth one is a bill quietly getting bigger.
